title: How to Plan a Holiday That's Better for the Planet
paragraphs: Many people love to travel, but travel can be bad for the environment. Flying, in particular, produces a lot of greenhouse gases. So how can people plan a holiday that is better for the planet? Experts offer several ideas.

First, think about what you really want from your holiday. Sarah Barfield Marks, a researcher who studies holidays without flying, wrote in The Conversation in 2026 that people should first ask what they want from a trip, such as warm weather, rest, adventure or time with family. Then, they can look for places that offer these things and are easy to reach without flying.

Second, take the train if you can. According to the consumer group Which?, taking the Eurostar train from London to Brussels instead of flying can cut emissions by 94%. However, trains are not always cheap. For example, a Greenpeace report found that taking the train from London to Edinburgh costs about 60% more on average than flying.

Third, if you need to fly, choose direct flights. Planes use a lot of fuel when they take off and land, so flights with stops usually produce more emissions. Also, business and first class seats can produce up to four times more carbon dioxide per passenger than economy seats. Which? also suggests taking fewer trips that involve flying, but staying longer.

Fourth, think about what you do at your destination. Walking, cycling and using public transportation are better than using cars. Spending money at small local businesses can also help local people. In addition, avoiding buffets can reduce food waste, because about half of buffet food is thought to be thrown away.
Finally, consider visiting less popular places instead. This can help reduce the problems caused by too many tourists in famous cities.
